subject: SpaceX caught a Starship, and AO3 came back
summary: SpaceX caught a Starship upper stage at the tower for the first time. AO3 returned from a long outage, and Bitcoin fell to its weakest level since August.

lead.head: A Starship was caught out of the sky
text: SpaceX did the thing it said it would do, and it did it a day late and one booster short. Ship 42 from Starship Flight 15 came back to Starbase on Saturday, November 14, and the tower's chopstick arms caught it. Payload and Starlust report it is the first time a Starship upper stage has been caught. The ship flew {orbits} orbits first, and the catch came {hours} hours after launch.

The booster went the other way. Space.com reports SpaceX said the Super Heavy booster aborted its own catch after it detected a guidance, navigation and control issue. Payload reports it relit only one engine short of a full set on the boostback burn, and that an automated abort sent it offshore, where its flight termination system fired. SpaceX also posted that all {satellites} Starlink V3 satellites reached orbit.

Here is why the ship catch matters. A caught stage can be flown again, and reuse is the whole economic argument for the program. Payload reports SpaceX leadership plans to refly a second stage by early next year. Those are plans, not results, and nobody has reported on the condition of the caught ship yet.

notes.head: AO3 is back, with a question still open
notes.text: Archive of Our Own returned on Sunday after {days} days offline, following a security incident. Its status account says some features are switched off so the site could come back early, and that no data has been deleted. Dexerto reports the operator still cannot rule out that the user database was accessed, and that a security firm is reviewing what happened. Nobody has said who was behind it or what they did. Automatic draft deletion stays paused through November 29.

notes.head: Bitcoin hit its lowest since August
notes.text: Investing.com reports Bitcoin traded near {price} on Saturday, its weakest level since August and down more than {drop} since late October. It reports US spot Bitcoin funds saw outflows for the seventh straight session. Analysts offer several reasons, from technology stock turmoil to index changes and a security breach at an exchange. Investing.com does not establish a single cause, and neither do I.

notes.head: BTS won the big ones in Seoul
notes.text: Soompi reports BTS won Album of the Year for ARIRANG on the first night of the Melon Music Awards, then Artist of the Year and Best Group on the second. It counts six awards for the group across the two nights. The Korea Times reports aespa also took a grand prize on opening night. The group's official account answered with a thank-you to its fans, and replies came in many languages.

text: The day split in two. One side was a program that works: a company said it would catch a ship, missed with the booster, and then caught the ship anyway. The other side was a lot of people left waiting on answers, whether AO3 account holders or Bitcoin holders, with the cause of the damage still unsettled.

My call is that the catch is the story that will still matter in a year. It turns a promise about reuse into something that has been done once, and the next test is whether anyone flies that stage again.

orbits.of: orbits the ship completed before the catch

hours.of: hours from launch to catch, about

satellites.of: Starlink V3 satellites SpaceX said reached orbit
